name: Reza Pahlavi
role: Exiled former crown prince of Iran and opposition leader; head of the House of Pahlavi; leader of the Iranian transition movement (Lion and Sun Revolution)
summary: Pahlavi advocates replacing the Islamic Republic with a secular, democratic Iran based on four principles: territorial integrity, separation of religion and state, individual liberties and equality of all citizens, and a free choice of the form of government (republic or constitutional monarchy) by referendum after a constituent assembly. His economic programme favours markets, private property, an independent central bank and integration into the global economy, and he supports maximum pressure and, since 2026, military strikes on the regime's repressive apparatus.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: His plan keeps a unified professional national army to defend territorial integrity.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The fourth principle of his economic programme is respect for private property and its safeguarding, which rules out state ownership of all land.

ban-cartels.rationale: The charter he co-signed pledges to abolish all economic monopolies, and the IPP plans proceedings on monopoly dissolution of regime-linked conglomerates.

bound-labor.rationale: He cited the condition of peasants as 'effectively serfs' as part of the backwardness that reform had to overcome.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Principle seven: controlling inflation requires fiscal discipline and an independent central bank; the IPP gives the central bank full functional independence and a price-stability mandate.

central-planning.rationale: He holds that Iran's stagnation came from ignoring economics and bases his programme on market mechanisms, private property and an independent central bank; he calls the regime's economy a failure and nowhere argues for central planning.

clerical-rule.rationale: He seeks to end the clerical government and replace it with a secular democracy.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The charter he co-signed commits Iran to join ILO conventions covering collective bargaining agreements; it does not say these replace individual contracts.

collective-defense.rationale: He called Sweden's NATO accession correct and necessary and said Sweden now stands inside NATO's collective defence.

conscription.rationale: The IPP transition plan keeps the conscription and military service organization after reform and professionalization; it is a transitional-phase provision.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He says sovereignty must return to the Iranian people, that the nation's vote is the final authority, and that no decision on borders or resources is legitimate without the people's consent.

constituent-assembly.rationale: He repeatedly says a constituent assembly should be elected and a new constitution then be put to a referendum; his transition decree provides for it.

death-penalty.rationale: The charter he co-signed commits to abolish the death penalty and the council he led opposed it as an instrument of state policy; his programme sets up fair trials of regime perpetrators rather than a stated sentencing policy.

democracy-best.rationale: He argues that democracy is the path to Iran's salvation, wants the people to choose the form of government by vote, and says he accepts whichever they pick (republic or constitutional monarchy); he did not speak to voters choosing badly.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: He says Iranian women have fewer legal rights and must navigate outdated notions of a woman's role, and that freedom starts with true equality for women.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Stresses that Iran's diverse ethnicities and religions have lived side by side and calls for national unity.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He says authority lies with the nation's sovereignty and vote, against religious rule.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The IPP programme he released says fundamental individual rights and freedoms grounded in the UDHR will be enshrined and inviolable in the new constitution and all laws, whichever system voters choose.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality of all citizens before the law and individual liberties is one of his four core principles; the charter he co-signed gives citizens of all beliefs, ethnicities, gender and sexual orientation equal dignity and rights before the law.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: He said some global interests would rather set the country alight so as to create 'statelets' they could dominate, and warned of opportunists with 'covetous eyes on Iran's soil'.

free-trade.rationale: He says a democratic Iran will open its economy to trade and investment and must rejoin the global economy; he did not say trade benefits everyone.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: He says Iran's nuclear programme should be totally dismantled and that it has no need to weaponize it.

independent-unions.rationale: The charter he co-signed commits to ILO conventions on freedom of assembly and the right to form organizations; he did not speak of union independence from the state in those words.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The charter he co-signed commits Iran to join the ICC and he calls for legal action abroad against those responsible for crimes against humanity; his main mechanism is a domestic transitional court.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: He calls internet shutdowns a sign of the regime's panic, demands unrestricted internet access and cyber measures to defeat blackouts, and condemns shutdowns and filtering (the panic remark is reported in Wikipedia).

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He says Cyrus freed the Jews to return to their homeland, pledges immediate recognition of the State of Israel and calls partnership with Israel critical.

land-redistribution.rationale: In a 2022 statement he counted his father's land reform as a step in the constitutional project because much of the population had been effectively serfs; this is a historical endorsement, not a statement of present policy.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He rejects sharia as the source of law, saying religious rule placed the authority of sharia above law and national sovereignty and calling for complete separation of religion from government.

limit-growth.rationale: He makes growth central: productivity should be the engine of growth and he laments two decades without measurable growth; he sets no environmental limit on it.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: His own ten principles say market mechanisms should guide economic interactions between citizens wherever possible and that policy should trust citizens' own decisions; he adds that government must create opportunity and remove barriers.

military-guardian-role.rationale: His programme enforces strict separation of the military from politics and civilian command of the army; the charter limits the military to defending territorial integrity.

minority-language-support.rationale: The charter he co-signed pledges to accept the position of native languages under international conventions; he gave no detail on schools or services.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Says Iranians should choose between a constitutional monarchy and a republic by referendum, and that he would hold only a transitional role; his own preference is contested in reporting.

nation-first.rationale: Mixed: he says cooperation with the world will be guided by Iran's national interests, but also stresses partnership, normalized ties and integration with the West and regional neighbours.

national-self-determination.rationale: Mixed: he insists on the Iranian people's right to self-rule and sovereignty (and Afghans' right to choose their system), but rejects separation of Iranian minorities, naming territorial integrity as non-negotiable.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The charter pledges to abolish all economic monopolies and confront organized corruption, and he denounces nepotism and graft by the regime's insiders.

no-central-bank.rationale: In his September 2024 keynote he lists, as the seventh principle of his economic programme, establishing an independent central bank to control inflation.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: He criticizes Iraq's sect-based political order and warns that Shia-Sunni sectarianism threatens Iran's unity.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The IPP programme repeals laws mandating religious indoctrination and ideological content in school curricula; it does not address every form of religious instruction.

one-party-rule.rationale: He seeks free competitive elections and a coalition of left and right, republicans and monarchists, and denounces the regime's single-ideology rule.

party-commands-army.rationale: His programme places the army under civilian command with strict civil-military separation and dissolves ideological forces such as the IRGC.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He calls protecting Iran's cultural and natural heritage a permanent national duty and criticizes imposing an 'inauthentic Western construct' on a society with its own traditions and norms.

private-courts-defense.rationale: His transition plan sets up a public Transitional Justice Court, an independent judiciary and a unified national army; it contemplates no privatized courts, police or defence.

property-fundamental.rationale: Principle four of his economic programme: a dynamic economy depends on respecting private property and safeguarding it from interference; the IPP lists it among its ten principles. He did not say how hard it should be to override.

public-ownership.rationale: His programme (IPP booklet) orders an audit of state-owned enterprises and a framework and priority list for privatizing them, and his principles favour markets and private property; it does not specifically address energy, rail and utilities.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The council he led treated prison terms for 'insulting Islamic sanctities' as persecution of prisoners of conscience; he also guarantees religious freedom for every citizen.

religious-nation.rationale: He says every Iranian, whatever religion or none, will be equal before the law, and describes a coalition inclusive of every group and faith.

religious-offensive-war.rationale: He denounces the Islamic Republic for spreading a radical caliphate across the region through aimless conflicts and wants Iran a nation-state with no foreign wars.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: The charter he co-signed promises citizens of all ethnicities dignity and equal rights before the law and acceptance of diversity in ethnicity, and he urged unity with ethnic minorities, which excludes expelling any of them.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The charter he co-signed guarantees the right to strike, and he called the truckers' strike just and 'a right step'; he voiced no wish to restrict strikes.

right-to-secede.rationale: Territorial integrity is the first of his four core principles, and he urged minorities not to use the war to press for separation.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He promises prosecution of those who killed protesters, a Transitional Justice Court and a truth commission, with fair trials.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Mixed: he says a free Iran seeks 'foreign investment, not foreign aid' and partnership rather than funding, but he actively invites foreign investment, which the statement also rules out.

separate-church-state.rationale: He names a clear separation of religion from state as a core principle and a prerequisite to democracy, and says it is among his first principles.

separated-powers.rationale: The IPP transition programme lists separation of powers and an independent judiciary among the principles that would be immutable in the new constitution under either form of government.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He insists on the rule of law and the nation's will as the basis of government and lists the rule of law among the immutable principles of a new constitution.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: He calls for abolishing the IRGC and dissolving the Basij and parallel armed structures, and (per Wikipedia) for expelling Iraqi militias from Iran.

state-harmful.rationale: He builds his programme on a transitional government, army, judiciary and elected parliament, and praises the construction of state institutions; he does not call the state unnecessary.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He demands release of all political prisoners and free elections, and condemns the regime's repression of dissent and independent groups.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He wants Iran returned to being a nation-state that spends no blood or treasure on foreign wars, and says Iranians want a government that does not spend blood or treasure on foreign wars; the charter commits Iran to cease interference in other countries.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: The charter he co-signed commits Iran to join the UN Convention Against Torture and to ban arbitrary arrests and detentions during the transition.

total-state.rationale: His programme de-ideologizes education, repeals laws imposing religious indoctrination and rests the economy on markets and individual liberty.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: He says Iran has been a nation-state for more than two millennia and invokes the continuity of its civilization from Cyrus the Great.

unions-good.rationale: He co-signed a charter committing to ILO conventions on freedom to form organizations, the right to strike and collective bargaining, and called the truckers' strike a just 'right step'.

women-must-cover.rationale: He condemns compulsory hijab and the hijab law as oppression; his programme makes hijab optional for students and teachers and abolishes rigid Islamic dress codes.

women-suffrage.rationale: He says one cannot speak of a modern society when women were barred from political participation and praises moves to include them.

notes: Living person; no inference. Positions on the monarchy itself are deliberately null: he says the form of government is for voters and has not stated a personal preference in the sources reviewed. Positions on sanctions and military action changed: in 2010-2011 speeches he opposed military strikes, while in 2025-2026 he welcomed US and Israeli strikes on the regime and urged more; the latest position is used. Mahsa Charter (March 2023) is a co-signed alliance document whose alliance later fell apart; his later four principles omit its decentralization pledge, so decentralization is only medium. The IPP booklet is written by expert authors under his leadership and treated as his programme.  Books and several press pages could not be reached (see notFound). 2026-11-12 pass: re-read the saved texts of his statements, speeches, interviews and the IPP booklet against every statement; added a stated answer where one existed (independent central bank, private property, equal rights across ethnic groups, torture convention, no religious war) and left the rest null. Themes searched: federalism, marriage, citizenship, immigration, climate, taxes, jury trial, technology, democracy promotion.
